comparator.name: Marine Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current BMS handbook: 135 EC compulsory taught study, 3 EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, 12 EC thesis and 30 EC open electives. Use one generic pathway, without a named track. MAT14803 is the first-listed restricted option, suitable for the stated Mathematics A preparation; it precedes MAT15103. MAT15403 assumes active high-school statistics or MAT15303. Complete all 138 prescribed taught credits, including all 60 first-year credits and MAE21306, before the thesis; this exceeds the 102-credit minimum. Complete the BC&PL portfolio and coordinator/adviser knowledge check. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are additional zero-credit obligations, not invented EC. Formal entry rules are distinguished from advisory assumed-knowledge references; renamed mathematics references in MAE21306 are not additional credits.

components.name: Boundary Crossing and Personal Leadership in Marine Sciences
components.note: The 3-credit course includes a core and a learning ribbon across six required courses, ending during the thesis. Passing its portfolio is required for the thesis grade; these are not extra credits.

components.name: Global Water Systems and Climate Change
Research Methodology for Human Environment Interactions
Field Project Marine Sciences
components.note: Integrated marine field research includes intertidal sampling, sediment transport, fish ecology and observations of Wadden Sea uses. Laboratory and fieldwork safety are required; BMS students have admission priority.

components.name: Introduction to Law for the Life and Social Sciences
Global Marine Compounds, Flows, and Cycles
Life History and Biology of Aquatic Animals
Evaluation and Design of Marine Nature-Based Solutions
Research Methods for Marine Sciences
components.note: Research design, marine sampling and monitoring, data analysis and a multi-day overseas field practical. Laboratory and fieldwork safety are required.

components.name: Assessment of Marine Nature Based Solutions
Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: Three-credit restricted choice between Mathematics Applied: Introduction and Statistics 1. This example takes the first-listed Mathematics Applied: Introduction, for a student with Mathematics A preparation; it precedes Mathematics Applied: Analysis. Statistics 2 assumes active high-school statistics or Statistics 1.

components.name: BSc Thesis Marine Sciences
components.note: Required 12-credit individual research thesis, with a proposal, research, report, presentation and defence. Entry requires at least 102 programme credits, all 60 first-year credits and Research Methods for Marine Sciences; the coordinator checks preparation with the study adviser. The boundary-crossing and personal-leadership portfolio must also pass.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Thirty open credits can be used for a minor and/or individual electives. No particular minor, placement or specialist package is assumed.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest response materially addresses marine ecological systems and their coastal, food-production, social and governance connections through actual UCR content. Only after accepting it, the biological conservation concept is accepted with evolution, molecular/biochemical study and quantitative investigation. Only then the coastal climate/spatial/energy concept is accepted with physical systems, data and intervention appraisal. All pass qualitative distinctness and the pairwise floor. Stop at the three-alternative maximum. Dedicated aquaculture, marine organismal field training, advanced ocean circulation and a required marine thesis remain limitations.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Shared evolutionary genetics, variation, selection and adaptation form a direct substantive relationship; the scope and credit weights differ.
Shared population/community ecology, food webs and ecosystem processes provide a direct ecological foundation.
Shared marine and estuarine organisms, habitats, ecological processes and human pressures; WUR additionally includes specific field practicals and excursions.

Both examine environmental effects and sustainability of biological food-production systems, including aquaculture. UCR is predominantly comparative farming; WUR integrates seafood supply, trade and governance.
Both substantively address molecular/cellular organisation, membranes, signalling and regulation. WUR includes its own laboratory applications.

The selected general biodiversity survey does not adequately reproduce this dedicated marine-organism adaptation, dissection and intertidal-field component. The strongest marine course already represents Marine Ecology; preserve this distinct specialist gap.

Shared water/compound chemistry, carbonate and nutrient/contaminant processes support part of the flows-and-cycles component. Ocean currents, tides, sediment transport and integrated marine socio-economics are additional WUR scope.
Both develop nature-based coastal/water interventions that combine ecosystem function with human goals; WUR uses a dedicated marine evaluation/design framework and design pitch.

Shared appraisal of coastal/delta water responses, ecological effects and trade-offs directly addresses part of nature-based-solution assessment. WUR adds modelled scenarios and integrated ecosystem-service reports.
Shared climate impacts, sea-level rise and adaptation/mitigation connect climate to water and marine systems; WUR adds explicit hydrological flows and a marine-case systems analysis.
Market failure, externalities, public goods and policy appraisal are substantive shared economic tools. WUR applies resource-economics concepts to fisheries, conservation and competing ocean uses.
Shared legal systems, legal reasoning and case-law analysis provide a meaningful introductory law relationship; WUR focuses on rules and scientific evidence for life/marine sciences.
Both directly analyse institutions, resource users, participation and policy at multiple scales. WUR dedicates the component to ocean/coastal governance.
Shared inference, hypothesis tests and regression are specific statistical content, with different mathematical depth and applications.
Shared research design and qualitative sampling/interview/observation methods support human-environment inquiry. WUR specifically develops a complete research proposal and combines strategies.
Shared differentiation, integration and differential equations provide direct mathematical content; the UCR course includes additional modelling and computational work.

Shared statistical model fitting, classification, validation and data-science analysis address a specific part of WUR modelling. UCR does not reproduce coupled ecosystem, economic and spatial simulation.
Shared geospatial data, projections, queries, transformations, terrain/surface analysis and remote sensing provide a direct GIS relationship.

audience.programmeDescription: Marine Sciences studies oceans, seas and coasts as linked ecological, physical and social systems. WUR combines marine biology and food systems with climate, economics, governance, spatial methods and the design of sustainable solutions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: These UCR programmes approach marine and coastal questions through different combinations of biology, environmental science, data, economics and governance. WUR offers a more extensive specialist marine sequence, including dedicated field courses, aquatic-animal and aquaculture study, ocean processes and a required marine thesis. UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits; a marine project is not guaranteed.
